newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran's new Russian submarine enters its waters.
newsitem.headline: Iran's new Russian submarine enters its waters.

text.p: Iran's new Russian-made submarine, which will boost the Islamic republic's naval power in the Gulf, has cruised into Iranian waters, a Western military official said on Sunday.
"It is in their waters and has been there throughout the night," the official, who requested anonymity, told Reuters. "It is in their territorial waters near Bandar Abbas."
He said the vessel was flying a Russian flag and was escorted by a Russian vessel: "There is no idea when they will shift the flag over."
The submarine left Russia for Iran in November and passed through Egypt's Suez Canal on January 2.

Non-Arab Iran already has two Russian-made submarines and analysts say it has poured billions of dollars into its navy since the end of the eight-year Iran-Iraq war in 1988. That has raised concerns in oil-rich Gulf Arab states, which the United States has vowed to protect.
Iran, which has said arms purchases are for self-defence, is the only Gulf state with submarines. The first of the three submarines was delivered to Iran in November 1992 and the second in June 1993.
Military analysts said the new ship would enhance Iran's ability to control Gulf waterways. It can lay mines and fire torpedoes against ships in the world's largest oil-export route.
The United States, which has waged a political and economic campaign to isolate Iran, has accused Tehran of using terrorism and says it poses a threat to regional security.
Iran rejects the accusations and accuses Washington of fueling Gulf Arab fears to sell billions of dollars of arms to its regional allies.

U.S. officials say Iran has restored its ability to fire anti-ship missiles at sea, has tripled the number of missiles on its Gulf coast in the last two years and is fitting Chinese-built cruise missiles on up to 20 naval boats.
Iran's forces include 513,000 active personel, missiles, destroyers, frigates, and coastal and patrol craft.
The United States has in the Gulf about 20,000 troops and 24 ships, including cruisers, destroyers and at least one submarine.
